environmental.title: Environmental Impact
environmental.description: By washing this item at an appropriate frequency, you are saving the above resources and reducing environmental impact.

washInfo.title: About Wash Reduction Calculation
washInfo.description1: Environmental impact calculation is based on the difference between actual wash count and "washing every time you wear" scenario.
washInfo.description2: However, it's common to wash multiple items at once. Therefore, the reduced wash count is divided by the average number of items per wash (5 items).
washInfo.example: Example: If worn 10 times and washed 2 times, theoretically 8 washes were reduced, but considering 5 items per wash on average, the actual reduction effect is 8÷5=1.6 washes.

waterInfo.title: About Water Usage (Cost) Calculation
waterInfo.description1: Water savings are calculated by multiplying the reduced wash count by the average water usage per wash (about 65 liters).
waterInfo.description2: Costs vary by region, but are calculated based on typical water rates (about $3 per 1000 liters).
waterInfo.example: Example: If 10 washes were reduced, 65 liters × 10 washes = 650 liters of water saved, which translates to about $1.95 in savings.

energyInfo.title: About Energy Usage (Cost) Calculation
energyInfo.description1: Energy savings are calculated by multiplying the reduced wash count by the average energy usage per wash (about 0.9 kWh).
energyInfo.description2: Costs vary by power company and contract plan, but are calculated based on typical electricity rates (about $0.25 per kWh).
energyInfo.example: Example: If 10 washes were reduced, 0.9 kWh × 10 washes = 9 kWh of electricity saved, which translates to about $2.25 in savings.

co2Info.title: About CO2 Reduction Calculation
co2Info.description1: CO2 reduction is calculated by multiplying the saved electricity by the CO2 emission factor for electricity (about 0.6 kg per kWh).
co2Info.description2: This considers not only washing machine usage, but also CO2 emissions related to water supply and treatment.
co2Info.example: Example: If 9 kWh of electricity was saved, 9 kWh × 0.6 kg/kWh = 5.4 kg of CO2 emissions were reduced.

impact.environmentalText: Through improving your washing habits, you have reduced {{co2}}kg of CO2 emissions. This is equivalent to the amount of CO2 absorbed by approximately {{treeEquivalent}} trees in one year.

washInfo.title: About Wash Count Reduction Calculation
washInfo.content1: Environmental impact calculations are based on the difference in actual wash counts compared to washing after every wear.
washInfo.content2: However, it's common to wash multiple items together. Therefore, reduced wash counts are divided by the average number of items per wash cycle (5 items).
washInfo.content3: Example: If worn 10 times and washed 2 times, theoretically 8 washes were reduced. But considering an average of 5 items per wash, the actual reduction effect is 8÷5=1.6 wash cycles.

waterInfo.title: About Water Usage (Cost) Calculation
waterInfo.content1: Water savings are calculated by multiplying reduced wash counts by the average water usage per wash (approximately 50 liters).
waterInfo.content2: Costs vary by region, but calculations are based on typical water rates (approximately ¥300 per 1000 liters).
waterInfo.content3: Example: Reducing 10 wash cycles saves 50L×10=500L of water, equivalent to approximately ¥150 in savings.

energyInfo.title: About Electricity Usage (Cost) Calculation
energyInfo.content1: Electricity savings are calculated by multiplying reduced wash counts by the average power consumption per wash (approximately 0.5kWh).
energyInfo.content2: Costs vary by power company and plan, but calculations are based on typical electricity rates (approximately ¥25 per kWh).
energyInfo.content3: Example: Reducing 10 wash cycles saves 0.5kWh×10=5kWh of electricity, equivalent to approximately ¥125 in savings.

co2Info.title: About CO2 Reduction Calculation
co2Info.content1: CO2 reduction is calculated by multiplying saved electricity by the CO2 emission factor for electricity (approximately 0.5kg per kWh).
co2Info.content2: This considers not only washing machine usage but also CO2 emissions related to water supply and treatment.
co2Info.content3: Example: Saving 5kWh of electricity reduces 5kWh×0.5kg/kWh=2.5kg of CO2 emissions.

treeInfo.title: About Tree Equivalent Effect Calculation
treeInfo.content1: Tree equivalent effect is calculated by dividing reduced CO2 emissions by the amount of CO2 one tree absorbs per year (approximately 20kg).
treeInfo.content2: This value shows how your improved washing habits have the same CO2 absorption effect as planting a certain number of trees.
treeInfo.content3: Example: Reducing 10kg of CO2 emissions has the same effect as planting 10kg÷20kg/tree=0.5 trees.

detergentInfo.title: About Detergent Usage (Cost) Calculation
detergentInfo.content1: Detergent savings are calculated by multiplying reduced wash counts by the average detergent usage per wash (approximately 30ml).
detergentInfo.content2: Costs vary by detergent type, but calculations are based on typical detergent prices (approximately ¥400 for 800ml bottle).
detergentInfo.content3: Example: Reducing 10 wash cycles saves 30ml×10=300ml of detergent, equivalent to approximately ¥150 in savings.

lifespanInfo.title: About Clothing Lifespan Extension Effect Calculation
lifespanInfo.content1: Clothing lifespan extension effect is calculated based on the reduction in wash counts. Generally, washing damages clothing fibers and causes fading and shape deterioration.
lifespanInfo.content2: Research shows that a 20% reduction in wash counts extends clothing lifespan by approximately 1.5 times. Based on this data, we estimate lifespan extension effects from reduced wash counts.
lifespanInfo.content3: Example: Reducing wash counts from 20 to 16 times (20% reduction) is estimated to extend clothing lifespan by approximately 1.5 times.
